description:
Company Overview:

We are building Protege to solve the biggest unmet need in AI — getting access to the right training data. The process today is time intensive, incredibly expensive, and often ends in failure. The Protege platform facilitates the secure, efficient, and privacy-centric exchange of AI training data.

Solving AI’s data problem is a generational opportunity. We’re backed by world-class investors and already powering partnerships with some of the most ambitious teams in AI. The company that succeeds will be one of the largest in AI — and in tech.

We’re a lean, fast-moving, high-trust team of builders who are obsessed with velocity and impact. Our culture is built for people who thrive on ambiguity, own outcomes, and want to shape the future of data and AI.

The role

Our infrastructure team runs the systems the rest of Protege depends on: cloud infrastructure, security, and IT. The data we hold is patient data, and the AI labs and health systems we work with check how we protect it before they work with us. We have strong security expectations and active compliance programs, but need a day-to-day owner for this work.

You’ll be our first dedicated security hire, and you’ll own the program end to end. This is a hands-on role. You’ll identify gaps in our AWS and Databricks environments and fix them yourself, run our SOC 2 and HIPAA compliance, review new systems and vendors, and lead the response when something goes wrong. You’ll work closely with our infrastructure and IT engineers, Legal, and every engineering team. The hard part is that you’re one person at a company that moves fast. Everyone here (including you) builds with AI tools and ships quickly, so you’ll have to pick the risks that matter most and fix them in ways that don’t slow the work down.

What you'll do

  • Find and fix our biggest security gaps. You threat-model and test our environments and platforms the way an attacker would, turn the results and scanner findings into a short list that matters, and close the top items yourself.

  • Run SOC 2, HIPAA, and other future compliance programs. Controls match how we work, evidence is collected automatically where it can be, and audits run without pulling engineers off their work.

  • Secure how data moves. Partner ingestion, de-identification, storage, and customer delivery each have access controls and logging you’d be comfortable showing a customer.

  • Review new systems, vendors, and AI tools. Teams get a clear answer in days, and security is part of a design before it ships.

  • Lead incident response. We have a tested plan, and when something happens you run it from triage through notification and review.

  • Handle customer and partner security reviews. Questionnaires and security calls get accurate answers backed by evidence.

  • Automate your own work. Evidence collection, monitoring, and reviews run on tooling you build, including with AI, so one person covers what usually takes a team.

What success looks like

  • 30 days: You’ve learned how data moves from partner to customer and where PHI sits, met Engineering, IT, Legal, and the teams that talk to customers, taken over incoming security questions and vendor reviews, and closed a first gap yourself.

  • 60 days: You’ve built the security roadmap, and you own it and our SOC 2 and HIPAA program end to end, with risks ranked and a plan agreed.

  • 90 days: You’ve closed the top risks on that roadmap, with results you can point to: the highest-risk gaps in our cloud and data platforms are fixed, and we’ve run an incident response exercise and acted on what it found.

What you'll bring

  • Owned security at a remote-first startup or fast-growing company, as the first security hire or one of a few

  • Found and fixed security problems yourself in a cloud environment, in code and configuration

  • Run a compliance program such as SOC 2, including evidence and working with auditors

  • Protected regulated or highly sensitive data, ideally health data under HIPAA

  • Responded to a real security incident and changed something afterward

  • Used AI tools as a core part of how you do security work

  • Explained risk to engineers, executives, and customers, and found a way to say yes

  • Nice to have: Secured a data platform such as Databricks, or systems that host and evaluate ML models
